chk_problem.reason: Both drafts identify the same core problem of the complexity and hardware expertise required for designing high-performance custom kernels.

chk_method.reason: Both drafts describe the same multi-agent system, MaxKernel, and its three paradigms.

chk_data.reason: Both drafts identify JaxBench (50 TPU kernel tasks) and workloads from open-source models as the datasets.

chk_setup.reason: Both drafts specify evaluations on TPU v6e hardware using MaxKernel's evaluation harness, with B adding a minor detail about XProf profiling.

chk_primary_result.reason: Both drafts report the exact same primary result of a 1.58× geometric mean speedup across JaxBench workloads.

chk_secondary_result.reason: Both drafts identify the 2.32× geometric mean speedup on production workloads, though A includes additional detail about outperforming human-written ones.

chk_baseline.reason: Both drafts list the XLA compiler and human-written Pallas kernels as baselines, with A including an additional zero-shot baseline.

chk_conclusion.reason: Both drafts conclude that agentic systems can successfully handle the complexities of low-level accelerator programming.

chk_limitation.reason: Draft A identifies a specific limitation of the Auto Agent (susceptibility to local optima), whereas Draft B suggests future directions/improvements rather than a limitation.
